about: The AP Statistics app pages. scripts/build-apstat.mjs writes each page's shell (head, header, footer, a <div id="app"> mount) from this file; the page's behavior is its script in statistics/assets/<script>, which mounts into #app. "static": true marks a generated page that is not an app (teachers.html). premium names the Premium feature (ApStatCore gates it); card is the line on the course home. No path may contain the token "ap" (docs/apstat-spec.md decision 2). tools[] are the ten trainers of docs/apstat-spec.md section 6, pre-registered in Phase 0: page statistics/tools/<slug>.html, script statistics/assets/tools/<slug>.js, model statistics/assets/tools/math/<slug>.js (ApStatMath.<camelSlug>), content statistics/data/tools/<slug>.json, validator scripts/lib/apstat-tool-checks/<slug>.mjs, test scripts/test/apstat-tool-<slug>.test.mjs (docs/apstat-architecture.md, "Tools"). topic is the tool's context topic: the tool is built only when its data file exists and that topic is published. FREE OR PREMIUM is set here and only here: a tool with "premium": "tools" is Premium; sampling-distributions, data-explorer and probability-trees carry none and are free (docs/apstat-spec.md section 6, proposed; owner to confirm).

apps.title: Practice questions
apps.desc: Statistics practice by unit, topic or skill: data sets in stimulus sets, numbers graded by table or technology, typed setups and conclusions in context.
apps.card: Drill a unit, a topic or a skill, with the probability and regression sets.

apps.title: Spaced review
apps.desc: Your statistics spaced review queue: every question you missed comes back just before you would forget it.
apps.card: Missed questions come back when you are about to forget them.

apps.title: Unit tests and practice exams
apps.desc: Timed statistics unit tests and full practice exams in the May 2027 format: 42 multiple-choice questions, then 4 free-response questions.
apps.card: Unit tests and full timed practice exams in the May 2027 format.

apps.title: Free-response practice
apps.desc: Statistics free-response practice in the four exam question types, 10 points each, with a rubric, a full-credit sample and a printable sheet.
apps.card: The four free-response question types, with 10-point rubrics and sample answers.

apps.title: Say it in context
apps.desc: Statistics conclusions and interpretations in context, built part by part, then an answer that earns the point beside one that does not.
apps.lede: Write a conclusion or an interpretation, then check it against the rubric and two model answers: one that earns the point and one that loses it.
apps.card: Conclusions and interpretations in context, checked against a rubric.

apps.title: Cram kit
apps.desc: Statistics cram plans counted back from your exam date: three or two weeks, day by day, weighted by unit, with unit sheets, timed mixed sets and practice exams.
apps.lede: A 3-week or 2-week plan counted back from your exam date, day by day: unit sheets and notes, a timed mixed set and one free-response question each study day, two full practice exams and rest days. Print it and tick the days off.
apps.card: 3-week and 2-week plans to exam day, and timed mixed sets.

apps.title: Flashcards
apps.desc: Spaced-repetition statistics flashcards built from the glossary, by unit and topic.

apps.title: Trainers
apps.desc: Statistics trainers: sampling distributions, data, sampling, experiments, probability, distributions, intervals, p-values, chi-square and regression.
apps.card: Trainers and simulators, then the questions about what you saw.

apps.title: Your dashboard
apps.desc: Your statistics mastery by unit, topic and skill, with every miss linked to the lesson that teaches it.
apps.card: Mastery by unit, topic and skill.

apps.title: Search the course
apps.desc: Search every statistics lesson, notes page, glossary term and tool in the course.

apps.title: For teachers
apps.desc: For statistics teachers: stable share links, printable notes and unit sheets, and sharing pages to Google Classroom, with no new student data collected.
apps.lede: Share any notes page, lesson or unit sheet with a stable link. Students need no account, and nothing they do leaves their device unless they choose to sign in.

tools.name: Data explorer
tools.title: Data Explorer
tools.desc: One data set as a dotplot, a histogram and a boxplot at once: drag a point and watch the mean and median, the SD and the IQR, and the outlier fences respond.
tools.blurb: Drag a point and watch the mean, median and spread respond.
tools.lede: Drag a value and watch every summary and graph respond.

tools.name: Sampling lab
tools.title: Sampling Lab
tools.desc: An illustrated population on a grid: draw simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic samples, see bias from convenience and voluntary response, and write a sampling procedure step by step.
tools.blurb: Draw four kinds of random sample and see where bias comes from.
tools.lede: Draw random samples four ways, then write the procedure.

tools.name: Design randomizer
tools.title: Design Randomizer
tools.desc: Experimental units, treatments, blocks and matched pairs: randomize with a seeded generator, check the balance, and name what random assignment allows.
tools.blurb: Randomize an experiment and see why it allows cause and effect.
tools.lede: Assign treatments at random, block, and name the design.

tools.name: Probability trees
tools.title: Probability Trees
tools.desc: The same events as a tree diagram, a two-way table and a Venn diagram, linked: conditional probability by slicing a row, independence checked, and a simulation closing in on the exact value.
tools.blurb: Slice a two-way table and watch conditional probability appear.
tools.lede: Build a tree, a table and a Venn diagram of the same events.

tools.name: Distribution areas
tools.title: Distribution Areas
tools.desc: Shade a region under a normal curve or a binomial histogram and read the probability: name the distribution, its parameters, the boundary and the direction, by table or technology.
tools.blurb: Shade the area and read the probability, normal or binomial.
tools.lede: Shade a region and read its probability, as the exam asks.

tools.name: Sampling distributions
tools.title: Sampling Distributions
tools.desc: Pick a population, a sample size and a statistic, then take one, a hundred or a thousand samples: the sampling distribution builds dot by dot, with its center and spread against the formulas and the Central Limit Theorem made visible.
tools.blurb: Watch a sampling distribution build, sample by sample.
tools.lede: Take samples and watch the distribution of the statistic build.

tools.name: Interval capture
tools.title: Interval Capture
tools.desc: A hundred confidence intervals from the same population, coloured by whether they capture the parameter: change the level and the sample size, see the margin of error, and pick the right interpretation.
tools.blurb: See what 95% confident really means, one hundred intervals at a time.
tools.lede: Build a hundred intervals and count how many capture the truth.

tools.name: p-value explorer
tools.title: P-Value Explorer
tools.desc: The null distribution with the observed statistic and the shaded p-value, one or two sided, then Type I and II errors and power with the alternative overlaid.
tools.blurb: Shade the p-value, then see Type I and II errors and power.
tools.lede: See where a p-value comes from and what power depends on.

tools.name: Chi-square lab
tools.title: Chi-Square Lab
tools.desc: A two-way table: expected counts cell by cell, each component on a heat map, and the chi-square statistic on its distribution with its degrees of freedom and p-value.
tools.blurb: Fill in expected counts and watch the chi-square statistic build.
tools.lede: Build a chi-square test from a two-way table, cell by cell.

tools.name: Regression lab
tools.title: Regression Lab
tools.desc: Drag points on a scatterplot: the least-squares line, r, r squared and the residual plot update live, with influential points and extrapolation shown, and slope and r squared interpreted in context.
tools.blurb: Drag points and watch the least-squares line and residuals respond.
tools.lede: Drag points and watch the regression line, r and residuals respond.
